record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Single-machine proportional deterioration and total tardiness
record.original_question: Given n jobs to be processed on a single machine, where job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = b_j t when it starts at time t and tardiness T_j = max(C_j - d_j, 0) relative to due date d_j, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total tardiness sum_j T_j. Is the problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, as conjectured from the fixed-processing-time counterpart, or is there a polynomial-time algorithm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem. There are n jobs J_1, ..., J_n to be processed without preemption on a single machine that can handle at most one job at a time. Each job J_j has a positive deterioration rate b_j > 0 and a due date d_j >= 0. If job J_j is started at time t >= t_0 (where t_0 > 0 is a fixed common starting time), then its processing time is p_j(t) = b_j t. A schedule is a permutation pi = (pi(1), ..., pi(n)) of the jobs; setting S_{pi(1)} = t_0, the start times and completion times satisfy S_{pi(k+1)} = C_{pi(k)} and C_{pi(k)} = S_{pi(k)} + b_{pi(k)} S_{pi(k)} = (1 + b_{pi(k)}) S_{pi(k)}. The tardiness of job J_j is T_j = max(C_j - d_j, 0). 

Determine the computational complexity of minimizing the total tardiness sum_{j=1}^n T_j over all permutations of the n jobs. Specifically, is this problem NP-hard (in the ordinary, binary sense), or does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm solving it?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2020 survey of time-dependent scheduling lists the single-machine proportional-deterioration total-tardiness problem as formally open. No subsequent publication encountered in the search establishes either NP-hardness or a polynomial-time algorithm for this specific variant, while the classical fixed-processing-time analogue 1||sum T_j is known to be NP-hard in the ordinary sense. The problem therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: New results for an open time-dependent scheduling problem
status_evidence.snippet: Open time-dependent scheduling problems are discussed; several variants with proportional deterioration remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Time-dependent single-machine scheduling problems with proportional deterioration include problems still considered open.

status_evidence.title: A special case of the single-machine total tardiness problem is NP-hard
status_evidence.snippet: The classical single-machine total tardiness problem 1||sum T_j is NP-hard in the ordinary sense.
status_evidence.claim: The fixed-processing-time counterpart 1||sum T_j is known to be ordinary NP-hard, motivating the conjecture for the proportional-deterioration version.
